name: @olai/kolu-client
//: HOW OLAI REACHES KOLU — see src/index.ts, which argues the whole boundary. What this manifest is FOR is the wall: a package cannot depend back on @olai/server, so the direction is physics rather than discipline.
//dependencies: @olai/surface is the vocabulary everything here produces, and it is the ONLY olai package this one names — which is the boundary as a fact rather than a comment. @olai/format is deliberately absent: the walk over the vault belongs to whoever holds the vault (@olai/server's claimants.ts), and what crosses into this package is four strings per claim (src/fleet.ts's Claimant). The @kolu/* this package imports — padi-client, solid-dockrow, surface, surface-daemon-supervisor, terminal-vocab — are absent from these dependencies for @olai/surface's reason (bunfig.toml): they are hydrated as raw TypeScript from the Nix store rather than installed from bun.lock, so they are declared once for the whole tree in the root package.json, and scripts/check-kolu-deps.sh keeps that list honest. WHAT IS NOT TRUE, and was asserted here until 2026-08-27: that this is the only olai package importing @kolu/*. Six do. The honest partition is two tiers — @kolu/surface* is a FRAMEWORK olai builds on and is imported anywhere, like effect; the PRODUCT tier (padi-client, terminal-vocab, detect) is the integration, and of that tier only padi-client and terminal-vocab are confined here. solid-dockrow is deliberately shared with @olai/web (fold here, render there), which the fifth debate sitting ruled when it retired the one-package ceremony. Nothing mechanical enforces any of this: no packages/*/package.json declares an @kolu/* dependency at all, so bun install cannot check it.
